page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.metal-24xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized server engineered for data-intensive and high-throughput workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors delivering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a 3.2 GHz base frequency. The CPU features 320 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX matrix accelerators. It lacks dedicated hardware GPUs, relying solely on CPU-based compute.

Memory and local storage capacity are primary features of this configuration. The instance provides 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage comprises 60,000 GB (60 TB) of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity directly attached to the host. External network connectivity operates with a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps, accommodating high-volume ingress and egress without virtual networking overhead.

Benchmark results place the multi-core compute and data processing capabilities of the i7ie.metal-24xl in the top tier. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,291.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 95,190.03, alongside top-decile ratings in database operations (33,739.36) and static web serving throughput (133.13 GB/sec). Memory throughput demonstrates strong performance, recording 289.33 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 117.71 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. CPU-based LLM prompt processing also reaches top-tier categories across medium and large models.

This server architecture balances massive local NVMe capacity with high DDR5 memory density and dedicated bare-metal CPU resources. The tradeoff lies in the absence of hardware accelerators for GPU-native pipelines. Consequently, the instance is best suited for large-scale relational or distributed databases, high-capacity search indices, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching clusters, and intensive ETL pipelines requiring direct physical hardware access.
